findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks wrong substring with inverted logic
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the prefix, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which straddles the token-type and grant shortcuts. It also returns false when that substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, which is the opposite of the intended check. Because the wrong substring almost never equals the shortcut, the matcher passes for any grant type. The integration tests therefore do not verify that the correct grant is encoded in the token ID.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: The constructor calls `requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so it checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is accepted silently and later encoded as the literal string "null" in the token ID.

findings.title: Token issuance fails for grant types without a registered factory
findings.body: `encodeTokenId` throws IllegalStateException when the grant type stored in the client session context has no known shortcut. That attribute is set from the raw `grant_type` form parameter. Any flow that sets an unrecognized grant type will now fail access-token creation with a 500 error. Examples are custom grants whose factory id differs from the grant_type value, or the legacy token exchange path. Consider falling back to UNKNOWN instead of throwing.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing custom grant type providers
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to the public SPI interface without a default implementation, so existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations no longer compile. The PR also removes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor, which breaks callers that use it. Separately, the javadoc says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters", but the decoder hard-requires exactly 2 characters. A custom grant with a 3-letter shortcut will produce token IDs that cannot be parsed.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut detection ineffective
findings.body: If two grants share a shortcut, `grantsByShortcuts` loses an entry while `grantsToShortcuts` keeps both, so the sizes differ and an error is thrown. However, the lazy refresh methods can later overwrite mappings without any validation. Duplicates introduced by grants deployed at runtime are therefore not detected, and decoding becomes ambiguous.
